brief.meaningEn: Do, buy or add more than is sensible for the situation.
brief.meaningZh: 在某情況下做得、買得或加得超過合理需要。
brief.grammar: Go overboard with something, go overboard on something, or go overboard without a complement. Went overboard is past tense; the phrase is figurative.
brief.register: Informal everyday advice; a friend helps plan a small farewell tea without making it extravagant.
brief.boundaryZh: 適量享受並非「過火」；要有超出預算、目的或合理程度的證據。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是從船上掉進水裏，也不是所有慶祝或購物都過度。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出原本合理的做法、過量的部分及其實際代價。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 179, row 9; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A small treat is fine, but do not go overboard.

listening.en: The class wanted a modest thank-you card, but then ordered a huge stage and hundreds of balloons. Their teacher said they had gone overboard for a ten-minute farewell.
listening.zh: 全班原本只想送一張簡單的感謝卡，後來卻訂了大型舞台和數百個氣球。老師說，為一場十分鐘的歡送會，這樣做有點過火。
listening.promptZh: gone overboard 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: They planned much more than the short event needed.
options.zh: 他們安排的東西遠超短活動所需。

options.en: They stayed within the original modest plan.
options.zh: 他們仍依照原本簡單的計劃。

options.en: The stage and balloons were essential to a ten-minute farewell.
options.zh: 大型舞台和數百氣球是十分鐘歡送會的必需品。

options.en: They cancelled the farewell entirely.
options.zh: 他們把歡送會完全取消。

listening.explanationZh: 大型舞台與數百氣球，相對十分鐘活動明顯過量。

reply.promptEn: Should Ravi buy twenty gift boxes for a dinner with four guests? Each guest needs only one small box, and the rest would use up the entire event budget.
reply.promptZh: （拉維要為只有四位賓客的晚餐買二十盒禮物嗎？每人只需一小盒，其餘會用盡整個活動預算。）

options.en: Four small boxes would meet the need.
options.zh: 四小盒已能滿足需要。

options.en: Twenty boxes exceed the number of guests and the budget.
options.zh: 二十盒超過賓客數目，亦超出預算。

options.en: Buying twenty boxes would be going overboard.
options.zh: 買二十盒會做得過火。

options.en: The extra sixteen boxes are unnecessary here.
options.zh: 多出的十六盒在此並不需要。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出二十盒對四人而言過量。

scene.promptZh: 小型讀書會只有六位參加者，主辦者卻租下可容五百人的禮堂，費用吃掉全年預算。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The organiser has gone overboard.
options.zh: 主辦者做得過火。

options.en: The organiser chose a room exactly suited to six people.
options.zh: 主辦者選了剛好適合六人的房間。

options.en: The venue costs nothing.
options.zh: 場地完全免費。

scene.explanationZh: 場地規模與費用都遠超需要。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法最不適合說 go overboard？

options.en: Buy two chairs for two people within budget.
options.zh: 在預算內為兩人買兩張椅子。

options.en: Order thirty cakes for four visitors when most will be thrown away.
options.zh: 為四位訪客訂三十個蛋糕，大多會被丟掉。

options.en: Cover every wall with costly decorations for a brief meeting.
options.zh: 為短會議花大錢裝飾每面牆。

contrast.explanationZh: 數量與預算都合理，沒有過量證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「一買蛋糕就是 go overboard。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Go overboard means excessive for the occasion; a suitable small cake may be perfectly reasonable.
options.zh: 做得過火要看是否超出場合需要；一個合適的小蛋糕可以很合理。

options.en: Any purchase is necessarily excessive.
options.zh: 任何購物必然過度。

options.en: Go overboard applies only when money is overspent, never when the amount is excessive.
options.zh: 做得過火只適用於超出金錢預算，數量過多卻不算。

dialogue.explanationZh: 關鍵是程度是否超過合理需要。

speaking.en: We can add flowers to the table, but let’s not go overboard and spend the whole month’s club budget on one dinner.
speaking.zh: 我們可以在桌上放花，但不要做得過火，把社團一整個月的預算花在一頓晚餐上。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出說話者接受甚麼、反對甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區舞蹈班有十二名學員，原定每人一瓶水。組織者卻想訂二百瓶並借用大型貨車運送，會超出運輸預算。用英文建議合適數量，並說明何處過量。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出十二名學員每人一瓶、二百瓶與大型貨車超出需要及運輸預算；不要說完全不用水。

examples.en: Twelve bottles would cover the twelve dancers, but ordering two hundred and hiring a large truck would go overboard and exceed the transport budget.
examples.zh: 十二瓶水足夠十二名舞蹈學員；訂二百瓶還借大型貨車就過火了，會超出運輸預算。

examples.en: For twelve dancers, the class needs one bottle per person, not two hundred. Bringing in a large truck for the surplus would go overboard and cost more than the transport budget allows.
examples.zh: 舞蹈班有十二名學員，每人只需一瓶水，而不是二百瓶。為多出的水借大型貨車會做得過火，並超出運輸預算。

takeaways.en: Go overboard means do more than a situation reasonably calls for.
takeaways.zh: 做得過火，指超出情況合理所需。

takeaways.en: A modest choice is not going overboard merely because it is optional.
takeaways.zh: 適量的非必需選擇，不一定就是做得過火。

brief.meaningEn: Informal name for shopping in hopes of feeling better. It is not clinical therapy and may or may not improve one’s mood.
brief.meaningZh: 非正式地指希望透過購物改善心情；並非臨床治療，效果也未必確定。
brief.grammar: Retail therapy is a noun phrase; “a little retail therapy” is common. It describes the motive for shopping, not the value or necessity of the item.
brief.register: Informal conversation among friends; a speaker explains a small purchase after a difficult week without claiming it treats distress.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是以購物轉換心情；買必需品、接受治療或純粹比較價格不一定是此意思。
brief.misconceptionZh: therapy 一字在此是輕鬆比喻，不是醫療建議，也不保證花錢後感覺更好。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分購物動機、實際結果及真正求助方式。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 179, row 11; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: She used a little retail therapy after a hard week.

listening.en: After a tiring week of rehearsals, Mei bought one inexpensive notebook simply because choosing it cheered her up. She joked that it was a little retail therapy.
listening.zh: 經過一週疲累的排練，美兒買了一本不貴的筆記本，只因挑選它令她心情好一點。她笑說這是小小的購物解悶。
listening.promptZh: retail therapy 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: She shopped to lift her mood.
options.zh: 她透過購物轉換心情。

options.en: She received professional psychological treatment.
options.zh: 她接受了專業心理治療。

options.en: She bought the notebook because it was required for rehearsal.
options.zh: 她因排練必需才買筆記本。

options.en: She was guaranteed to feel better permanently.
options.zh: 她保證會永久感覺更好。

listening.explanationZh: 她說挑選筆記本令自己稍微開心，並非接受治療。

reply.promptEn: Why did Ben browse the weekend bookstall? He had a disappointing day, wanted the pleasant experience of choosing a low-cost novel and was not shopping for a required textbook.
reply.promptZh: （阿賓為何逛週末書攤？他那天不如意，想藉挑一本便宜小說轉換心情，並不是要買必需課本。）

options.en: He wanted a small purchase to lift his mood.
options.zh: 他想透過小額購物改善心情。

options.en: He enjoyed browsing after a difficult day.
options.zh: 他在不如意的一天後享受逛書攤。

options.en: He was looking for a little retail therapy.
options.zh: 他想小小購物解悶。

options.en: Choosing a low-cost novel was his way of feeling better after that day.
options.zh: 挑一本便宜小說，是他在不如意的一天後轉換心情的方法。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均指出購物的轉換心情動機。

scene.promptZh: 朋友在緊張的演講後到市集挑了一張小明信片，說逛攤位讓她放鬆。哪句最貼切？

options.en: She enjoyed a little retail therapy.
options.zh: 她小小購物，轉換了心情。

options.en: She has completed a medical treatment.
options.zh: 她已完成醫療治療。

options.en: She purchased a compulsory work supply.
options.zh: 她購買了工作必需品。

scene.explanationZh: 購買小物與逛市集是為了舒緩心情。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情境最不像 retail therapy？

options.en: Someone buys a small plant after a hard day because browsing feels enjoyable.
options.zh: 有人因為逛店開心，在辛苦一天後買一盆小植物。

options.en: A parent buys prescribed medicine needed immediately, without any wish to shop for pleasure.
options.zh: 家長因急需而購買處方藥，完全不是為購物樂趣。

options.en: A student chooses an inexpensive scarf after exams to cheer herself up.
options.zh: 學生考試後挑一條便宜圍巾，讓自己開心一點。

contrast.explanationZh: 購買急需的藥物不是為購物轉換心情。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說：「retail therapy 就等於正式心理治療，而且一定有效。」你會怎樣回應？

options.en: Retail therapy is an informal shopping expression, not treatment or a guaranteed result.
options.zh: 購物解悶是非正式說法，並非治療，也不保證有效。

options.en: Any shopping trip replaces professional help.
options.zh: 任何購物都可代替專業協助。

options.en: Any low-cost purchase must improve a person’s mood.
options.zh: 任何低價購物都必定改善心情。

dialogue.explanationZh: 這裏的 therapy 是比喻用法。

speaking.en: I bought one cheap postcard as a bit of retail therapy after the long journey, but it was not a solution to every worry.
speaking.zh: 漫長旅程後，我買了一張便宜明信片，當作小小購物解悶；但這不能解決所有煩惱。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出說話者買了甚麼及沒有聲稱甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：阿玲因校園展覽準備得很累，週六逛二手書店，花三十元買一冊詩集，只因挑選過程令她放鬆；她仍須休息並完成展覽工作。用英文說明購物動機和限制，勿稱之為醫療治療。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出二手書店、三十元詩集、挑選令她放鬆、仍要休息及完成展覽工作。

examples.en: After exhausting exhibition preparations, Ling spent thirty dollars on a poetry book at a second-hand shop as a little retail therapy. Browsing helped her relax, but she still needed rest and had work to finish.
examples.zh: 準備展覽後感到疲累，玲在二手書店花三十元買詩集，當作小小購物解悶。逛店讓她放鬆，但她仍須休息並完成工作。

examples.en: Ling’s retail therapy was a thirty-dollar poetry book from a second-hand shop: choosing it after exhibition work felt relaxing, yet the purchase did not replace rest or finish her remaining tasks.
examples.zh: 玲以三十元在二手書店買詩集，當作購物解悶：展覽工作後挑書令她放鬆，但購物不能代替休息，也不能完成餘下任務。

takeaways.en: Retail therapy is informal shopping to try to feel better.
takeaways.zh: 購物解悶是為轉換心情而購物的非正式說法。

takeaways.en: Retail therapy is not clinical treatment or a guaranteed cure.
takeaways.zh: 購物解悶不是臨床治療，也不保證解決問題。
